summary: In this excerpt from Book 2, the narrator and Arthur talk with Courtney, a young woman who was rescued from a drug cartel. Courtney describes her sister Dawna as an amazing person who has given her a purpose, and says Dawna plans to change the world. The narrator challenges this, arguing that Dawna could have freed Courtney from the cartel directly and that Courtney is a pawn in Dawna's larger game. Courtney politely dismisses the offer of help and expresses her wish to join Dawna's work.
one_line: In Book 2, the narrator and Arthur question Courtney about her devoted sister Dawna, who claims to be working to change the world.
key_facts: Courtney says the narrator and Arthur are held in cells, which she describes as being 'for your own good'.
Courtney says her sister is helping the narrator and Arthur become better.
Courtney describes her sister Dawna as 'the most amazing person in the world'.
Courtney says she was 'so lost' before Dawna helped her.
Courtney says Dawna was not really her sister by blood, but she is her sister 'in every way that matters'.
Courtney says Dawna came to get her as soon as she could after the cartel snatched her.
The narrator says Dawna could have walked Courtney out of the cartel's custody if she had wanted to.
The narrator calls Courtney 'a pawn in some huge game' that Dawna is playing.
Courtney says Dawna is 'fixing everything', so there will be no faraway island and no running away.
Courtney says her life is going to have 'real meaning' by helping Dawna.
When asked what Dawna wants to do, Courtney answers 'Change the world.'
Courtney says Dawna and others are working to stop drug cartels, cruelty, starvation, and war.
Courtney says she hopes the narrator will help Dawna as well.
The narrator asks, 'Dawna's goal is to make the world a better place?' and Courtney blinks at the narrator in response.
